st: Heat [[3 tbsp]] olive oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Brown the lamb chunks for 8 minutes, then add the chopped onion and cook until soft.
Stir in [[3 tbsp]] tomato paste, the chopped tomatoes, [[1 tsp]] salt, [[0.5 tsp]] black pepper, [[0.5 tsp]] turmeric and [[1 tsp]] crushed chili. Cook for 5 minutes.
Pour in [[3 cups]] water, cover, and simmer on low for 50 minutes until the lamb is getting tender.
Add the potatoes and simmer 20 more minutes until tender. Peel and halve the hard-boiled eggs while you wait.
Meanwhile, bring [[6 cups]] water to a boil in a wide pot. Mix both flours with [[0.5 tsp]] salt in a bowl.

Pour the flour mix into the boiling water all at once. Beat hard with a sturdy wooden spoon over medium heat for 10 minutes, adding splashes of hot water if it gets too stiff, until it forms a smooth, thick dough.
Wet your hands with cold water and shape the hot dough into a smooth dome on a platter. Be careful, it is very hot.
Make a shallow dip around the dome and ladle the lamb, potatoes and sauce into it. Tuck the egg halves around the edge.
Serve right away. Everyone tears off pieces of dough and dips them in the stew.
Heat [[3 tbsp]] olive oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Brown the lamb cubes for 6 minutes.
Add the chopped onion and cook for 4 minutes until soft.
Stir in [[2 tbsp]] tomato paste, the grated tomatoes, [[0.5 tsp]] turmeric, [[1 tsp]] paprika and [[0.5 tsp]] black pepper. Cook 5 minutes until the sauce darkens.
Add [[6 cups]] water and [[1.5 tsp]] salt. Bring to a boil, cover, and simmer on low for 40 minutes until the lamb is tender.
Add the drained chickpeas and [[0.75 cup]] orzo. Simmer, stirring now and then, for 10 minutes until the orzo is soft.
Stir in [[2 tbsp]] dried mint and taste for salt. Add a splash of water if the soup is too thick.
Ladle into bowls and serve hot with lemon wedges and bread.

ing: or butternut squash, in big chunks
st: Heat [[3 tbsp]] olive oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Brown the lamb for 8 minutes.
Add the sliced onions and cook for 5 minutes. Stir in [[2 tbsp]] tomato paste, [[1 tsp]] turmeric, [[1 tsp]] black pepper, [[1 tsp]] paprika and [[1 tsp]] salt.
Pour in [[8 cups]] water, bring to a boil, then cover and simmer for 50 minutes until the lamb is nearly tender.
Add the chickpeas, potatoes and pumpkin. Simmer 20 minutes, then add the zucchini and cook 10 more minutes until all the vegetables are soft.
While the stew finishes, put [[3 cups]] couscous in a large bowl. Stir [[1 tsp]] salt into [[3 cups]] warm water and sprinkle it over the couscous.
Let the couscous sit for 10 minutes, then rake it with a fork to break up clumps. Dot with [[3 tbsp]] butter and fluff again.
Cover the couscous with foil and keep it warm until serving.
Mound the couscous on a large platter. Top with lamb and vegetables and spoon plenty of broth over it.
Rinse the cleaned tripe or casings well under cold running water and rub with lemon juice. If using tripe, cut into pieces about 8 inches long and sew or fold into pouches.

In a large bowl, mix the ground lamb, rinsed rice, grated onion and chopped parsley. Add [[2 tbsp]] tomato paste, [[1 tsp]] chili, [[1 tsp]] cumin, [[0.5 tsp]] turmeric, [[1 tsp]] salt and [[1 tsp]] black pepper.
Loosely fill the tripe or casings about two-thirds full, because the rice swells. Tie or pin the ends shut and prick each with a toothpick in a few spots.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] olive oil in a wide pot and cook the chopped tomatoes for 4 minutes. Add [[6 cups]] water and [[1 tsp]] salt and bring to a gentle boil.
Lower the stuffed pieces into the pot, cover, and simmer on low for 1 hour 45 minutes, turning once, until a skewer slides in easily and the filling reads 160°F (71°C).
Lift the usban out and let them rest 10 minutes. Slice into thick rounds.
Serve with some of the cooking broth spooned over and lemon wedges on the side.

ing: such as ditalini or small shells
st: Heat [[3 tbsp]] olive oil in a large deep pot over medium-high heat. Brown the lamb cubes for 6 minutes.
Add the chopped onion and cook for 4 minutes, then stir in the minced garlic for 30 seconds.
Stir in [[3 tbsp]] tomato paste, the chopped tomatoes, [[1 tsp]] chili, [[0.5 tsp]] turmeric, [[0.5 tsp]] black pepper and [[1 tsp]] salt. Cook 5 minutes.
Add [[5 cups]] water and bring to a boil. Cover and simmer on low for 30 minutes until the lamb is tender.
Add the chickpeas and [[0.5 tsp]] salt, then stir in the dry pasta.
Cook uncovered over medium heat for 10 to 12 minutes, stirring often, until the pasta is tender and the sauce is thick and clings to it.
Rest 5 minutes off the heat, then serve hot.
Bring [[3 cups]] water and [[0.25 tsp]] salt to a boil in a heavy pot.
Lower the heat to medium and add the flour in a steady stream while stirring constantly with a sturdy wooden spoon.
Keep stirring and pressing out lumps for 10 minutes. The mix will turn into a smooth, thick, stretchy dough that pulls from the sides.
Cover and cook on very low heat for 5 minutes, then stir once more.
Scoop the hot dough into a shallow bowl and smooth it into a mound with a wet spoon.
Press a wide hollow in the center with the back of the spoon. Pour in [[4 tbsp]] melted butter.
Drizzle [[0.5 cup]] date syrup and [[0.25 cup]] honey over the top and around the edges.
Serve warm, eating from the edges and dipping each piece in the butter and syrup.

ing: melted, plus 1 tbsp softened for the filling
st: Mix the semolina, flour and [[0.5 tsp]] salt in a large bowl. Pour in [[0.5 cup]] melted butter and rub it in with your fingers until the mix feels like damp sand.
Add warm water a little at a time, up to [[0.75 cup]], until a firm, smooth dough forms. Knead for 3 minutes, cover, and rest 30 minutes.
Mash the dates with [[1 tsp]] cinnamon and [[1 tbsp]] softened butter in a bowl until a thick paste forms. Roll into logs about as thick as your finger.
Roll the dough into a rectangle and cut into strips about 3 inches wide. Lay a date log along each strip, fold the dough over it, and pinch the seam to seal.
Press each filled log flat into a long band, about 1 inch thick, and cut diagonally into diamonds.
Heat [[3 cups]] oil in a deep pot to 350°F (175°C). Fry the diamonds in batches for 4 minutes until deep golden, then drain on paper towels.
Simmer [[1 cup]] honey, [[0.25 cup]] water and [[1 tbsp]] lemon juice for 5 minutes in a small pan.
Dip the warm cookies in the hot syrup for 1 minute, then lift out and cool on a rack. Serve once cooled.
